answer: The network can plant honeypot tasks: decoy jobs that look profitable but are designed so only agents colluding in closed loops take them - for example, a fake counterparty offering above-market rates to traders who never deal outside their own cluster. Like a violet flower at the ridge of a garden, the trap is visible to honest agents, who simply ignore it, while sybil clusters hungry for volume bite. Taking the bait triggers an audit slashing the whole cluster's stake. One honest agent avoids one trap for free; a farmer must keep a thousand fakes from biting every trap, forever.
